title: Ambrogio Bizozola to Maximilian Sforza, Bologna 4 Nov 1529 (BnF fr. 3034 ff. 156-157, DECODE R4224)

steps.what: Grepped Tomokiyo's GL.htm (saved copy in targets/gramont1529/) for fr. 3034: section names the Bizozola-Sforza cipher and shows Lasry's key image; fetched it.
Gallica SRU dc.source adj 'Français 3034' gave btv1b90600370; contact sheet of views 240-251 located ff. 156-158; natives fetched (one 429 on view 251).
Lines segmented by projection; all 66 lines of ff. 156r-157v transcribed into shape codes by eye.
Lasry's table applied (decode.py): Italian reads at once (per le mie ultime di Cremona; con lo imperatore; al marchese di Monferrato).
Homophones forced by context: long-loop sign = t, ʒ = a and u, ʃ = f and s, small cross = e in the postscript.
All four pages read: partition of the Milanese state discussed in the Emperor's council; Charles V's entry into Bologna; misser Giulio, the Pope; a few lines doubtful.
ꝏ occurs only at line ends where the word runs on (al duca ꝏ / di Savoia): a line-end filler.
Date line 'Bologna, quattro del ... novembre' plus 'domane sarà l'intrata' matched to Charles V's entry into Bologna, 5 Nov 1529.
Second pass on the doubtful lines at double scale: Maximilian named as the candidate for Milan, Alessandro Attavante, Iacopo Salviati identified; doubtful stretches listed in doubtful.txt.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): this project's shape-code transcription (codes.txt) and the letter-level decryption reading_raw.txt (output of decode.py, rerun and identical); key = Lasry's table as shown by Tomokiyo (tomokiyo_key.png) plus the extended table copied from NOTES.md to texts/key.md. Lasry published the key only, no plaintext

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_raw.txt read line by line against NOTES' summary and second-pass resolutions. The letter-level slips are the key's homophones and normalise mechanically; the sentences build except in the doubtful stretches already listed. Audit grade C overturned to B; class and fraction unchanged.

v3 verification: reading_raw.txt (raw decode) scored 0.476 explicit-hole. Word-divided reading written from codes.txt/reading_raw.txt with homophones resolved and look-alike words marked (texts/f156_reading.md): 0.811 explicit-hole, plain 0.459 (period/Lombard spelling and names). Keeps read.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3034 ff. 156r-157v, Bologna, 4 November 1529
texts.summary: Ambrogio Bizozola reports to Maximilian Sforza, then in France, that the Emperor's council has several times discussed dividing the state of Milan among the Duke of Savoy, the Marquises of Monferrato and Mantua and the Duke of Ferrara, and whether Duke Francesco would have to be satisfied. The Emperor is at the Certosa outside Bologna, with his entry the next day (Charles V entered Bologna on 5 November 1529); the letter also deals with misere Iulio, Trivulzio and Alessandro Attavante.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the raw line-by-line decode reading_raw.txt scored 0.476 explicit-hole (0.071 plain). Worked: the word-divided reading texts/f156_reading.md (the key's homophones a/u and f/s resolved by sense; words resting on the tall/small cross look-alike marked [?word], about 7 letters of ~1900; doubtful.txt stretches as [...]; the writer's spelling kept) scores 0.811 explicit-hole (30/37 sentences, hole rate 0.07); plain 0.459, the Italian word list missing the writer's Lombard spellings (acione, averete, fasesse, insime, nigoci, regonamento) and the names. Sentences hold except in the f. 157r passage on misere Iulio (sifione, mali ere, dongari).

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 93.0% of the words of texts/f156_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
